item.title: ILS delivers genuine diversification for alternatives allocations: Sage Advisory
item.description: Given most traditional alternative investments rely on the same economic drivers as the broader market, ILS highly differs because its returns are tied to natural catastrophe or insurance events rather than economic cycles, which leads Sage Advisory Services to say that investing in insurance-linked securities can achieve genuine diversification. However, he points out that insurance-linked securities offer investors access to a different risk premium entirely, “across a $144.5 billion market in which catastrophe bonds are the visible half and privately negotiated reinsurance is the broader one, tested on a contract calendar that does not negotiate.” “Most of what sits inside a typical alternatives allocation, whether private equity, private credit, real estate, or infrastructure, ultimately depends on the same small set of drivers. “Insurance-linked securities, or ILS, are one of the few allocations that genuinely do.

item.title: Bermuda’s BSX maintains global ILS listings leadership, takes majority of issuance through Q3
item.description: The Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) has now listed in total 169 new catastrophe bond notes and insurance-linked securities structures in the first three-quarters of 2026, maintaining its global position as ILS listings leader and becoming home to the vast majority of listed ILS issuance so far this year. A heavy maturity load and some more early redemptions of mortgage insurance-linked notes resulted in the total value of ILS listings on the Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) falling through the third-quarter of 2026. Having reached as high as $70.5 billion of ILS related listings on the exchange after the first-half of this year , the figure has declined slightly to almost $67.4 billion of cat bond and ILS listings on the BSX as of September 30th.

item.title: Hurricane Simon track remained outside of Mexico cat bond parametric trigger zones: Loconte
item.description: As major hurricane Simon’s path shifted west it appears to have remained offshore of the important parametric trigger zones related to the $175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) catastrophe bond, according to analysis by Isacco Loconte an insurance-linked securities (ILS) Investment Specialist at asset manager Azimut Switzerland SA. As we had been reporting over the weekend , hurricane Simon’s minimum central pressure, a critical factor in determining whether any payout would come due for the catastrophe bond, did deepen to a sufficiently low level to activate a payout should the storm’s track have crossed into any of the parametric trigger boxes. While those pressure levels were strong enough to meet the L1 payout threshold for the parametric zones, the hurricane trajectory worked in the bond’s favor.” Based on the parametric trigger design, hurricane Simon’s central pressure would have needed to be at 932mb or lower to activate a payout from the zones it came closest to.

item.title: NEXROC announces intention to acquire US and Australian insurance companies

item.description: According to the Best’s Market Segment Report, “MENA Reinsurers are Focused on Profitable Growth Opportunities Despite Heightened Geopolitical and Economic Uncertainties”, the growth potential for reinsurers is supported by adequate reinsurance pricing and emerging business opportunities, particularly in specialised risks. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) reinsurance market continues to present solid top-line growth opportunities and attract steady inflows of international capital, even as geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties intensify across the region, a new AM Best report states. Fleur Ngassa, financial analyst at AM Best and one of the report’s authors, said: “Despite uncertain times, some growth opportunities have emerged for reinsurers in the region.

item.title: PCRIC & UNDRR sign agreement to advance parametric solutions in the Pacific
item.description: The Pacific Catastrophe Risk Insurance Company (PCRIC), a provider of parametric disaster insurance, and the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) signed a Letter of Cooperation to strengthen their shared commitment to advancing disaster risk reduction and financial resilience across the Pacific region by advancing parametric insurance models to make them proactive resilience tools. By combining financial protection with proactive disaster management, we are ensuring that Pacific governments have both the liquidity and the foresight to respond effectively to disasters.” Marco Toscano-Rivalta, Chief, UNDRR Regional Office, Asia and the Pacific, added, “UNDRR is proud to join forces with PCRIC in advancing innovative and inclusive financing solutions that empower Pacific Island Countries to reduce risk and build resilience. Aholotu Palu, Chief Executive Officer, PCRIC, commented, “This partnership with UNDRR represents a significant step in embedding disaster risk financing into the broader resilience architecture of the Pacific.

item.title: Hurricane Simon forecast to near landfall as major storm, Mexico catastrophe bond at risk
item.description: Hurricane Simon in the Pacific remains a very strong storm at major hurricane strength and is expected to sustain that status when it nears landfall on the Mexico coastline on Sunday, with its intensification and deeper pressure now putting the $175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric catastrophe bond at potential risk. While some slight weakening could occur, Simon is still forecast to move near or over the coast of west-central Mexico as a major hurricane today.” As we’ve reported and you can see more on this by going through the original article and updates below, we understood from sources that a pressure of 932mb or lower may be the required threshold for a triggering event to occur in relation to Mexico’s catastrophe bond. That is now at a low enough level where Mexico’s $175 million tranche of IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric catastrophe bond notes are thought likely to face a triggering event and a 25% payout, should Simon cross the parametric trigger box line with pressure of 932mb or lower.

item.title: Hurricane Simon continues to intensify, Mexico catastrophe bond on watch
item.description: Hurricane Simon in the Pacific is rapidly intensifying and seen as having a chance of sustaining major hurricane strength when it makes landfall on the Mexico coastline on Sunday, which has brought the $175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric catastrophe bond back into focus again. Our sources suggest that hurricane Simon could now get closer to the low-levels of central pressure required to trigger Mexico’s parametric catastrophe bond. Mexico’s $175 million parametric IBRD Pacific named storm catastrophe bond is on watch again with this storm.

item.title: Flock Safety Will Cut Several Hundred Jobs Amid Surveillance Backlash
item.description: Flock Safety plans to let go of about 18% of its employees, people with direct knowledge of the plans said on Thursday, as the maker of AI-powered surveillance cameras and license-plate readers faces mounting opposition to its products from communities and lawmakers. The people said job cuts came after a voluntary buyout program and are expected to impact roughly 270 employees at Flock, a surveillance technology startup that has seen rapid growth in recent years. Home Depot investors recently demanded reviews of the retailer’s partnerships with surveillance technology vendors after reports that Flock’s data was used in immigration enforcement.

item.title: Satellites Study Hurricanes During El Niño
item.description: The satellite, flying 30 seconds behind its predecessor, Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich, provides precise sea level height measurements during what oceanographers expect to be a historic El Niño. The data each satellite collects will allow scientists to better understand this year’s El Niño and also help them create more accurate hurricane predictions. Ocean height varies from place to place and provides insight into the ocean’s heat content, and since warm water expands, that helps forecast how fast hurricanes will grow.

item.title: Aegon’s EGM approves redomiciliation and Omnibus Incentive Plan
item.description: Aegon Ltd., an international financial services holding company, has announced that its Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (EGM) approved both the redomiciliation and the Omnibus Incentive Plan proposal, authorising Aegon to proceed with its redomiciliation to the US. Aegon expects to proceed with the redomiciliation on 15 October 2026, with the repurchase of all outstanding Common Shares B held by Vereniging Aegon in exchange for common shares with equal voting rights on a 40-to-1 basis. During its Capital Markets Day in December 2025, Aegon announced plans to move its head office and legal seat to the United States.

item.title: Nuclear verdicts put US casualty exposures under fresh scrutiny: Munich Re
item.description: European businesses with exposure to the US may need to reassess their casualty risk as the frequency and size of so-called nuclear verdicts continue to present challenges for insurers, according to Munich Re, the global reinsurer. Nuclear verdicts, generally referring to jury awards above USD $10 million, remain a significant concern for the US casualty market. While European courts are unlikely to generate nuclear verdicts on the same scale as the US, Munich Re says European companies with American operations or commercial interests cannot afford to regard the issue as solely a US problem.

item.title: Trump’s Executive Order on Dyed Diesel Provides Little Relief for Farmers and Truckers
item.description: Farmers, truckers and economists say a move to cut taxes on diesel will provide little relief from record-high fuel prices that have soared since the U.S. Industry groups said they appreciate President Donald Trump’s executive order expanding the use of a diesel now reserved for off-road work, but farmers already have access to the fuel and many have already wrapped up harvest. The executive order defers the $0.24 federal tax per gallon of regular diesel, used for road projects, until the end of the year.

item.title: PVC Pipes Swept Away by Helene Still Dominate Cleanup of NC River
item.description: Canada-based IPEX would not say how many pipes were stored at its Woodfin, North Carolina, site before the storm or share results of a company-funded study of how much remains in the river, calling the information “commercially sensitive.” Officials said 60% of pipes stored outdoors at the site, sandwiched between railroad tracks and the river, were swept away by the 2024 flood, but most were recovered fairly quickly. Along the iconic French Broad River, known for its whitewater rapids, one item stands out from the rest: massive numbers of PVC pipes that washed away from a factory north of Asheville. “We still have stretches of river that haven’t been touched.” MountainTrue estimates its crews have pulled hundreds of thousands of pipes from the river — most of which went to landfills — with an untold number still littering the river for 70 miles (113 kilometers) to a large lake at the Tennessee border.
